title: Kotlin Naming and Style Conventions
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of kotlin naming and style conventions using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates kotlin naming and style conventions.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Kotlin Naming and Style Conventions** as part of **Kotlin Syntax and Basic Structure**. Readable names, focused functions, explicit ownership, and low-coupling module boundaries reduce maintenance cost. Use the subtopics—Classes and Objects, Functions and Properties, Constants, Packages, and Files—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Clear fundamentals help you reason about program behavior before adding abstraction. Small input/output checks make syntax and control flow easier to debug.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with classes and objects. Then compare it with functions and properties. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Classes and Objects
items.text: Classes and Objects should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.

items.title: Functions and Properties
items.text: Functions and Properties describes how behavior is declared, passed, or composed. Make inputs and return types clear, keep side effects visible, and use a small call-site example to judge readability.

items.title: Constants, Packages, and Files
items.text: Constants, Packages, and Files is part of reproducible project configuration. Declare the dependency or plugin where it belongs, preserve a compatible version set, and use the Gradle Wrapper for repeatable builds.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet in a Kotlin/JVM console project and run the configured Gradle application task, or use the Kotlin Playground for examples that need no external dependencies.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Kotlin Naming and Style Conventions removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
